permutationLabel: Hernia cause: strangulated femoral hernia (elderly, anticoagulated)
summary: 83-year-old woman on apixaban, 2 days of SBO and a tense, tender, irreducible right femoral lump with erythema; T 37.9 °C, HR 112, lactate 2.9; CT: incarcerated femoral hernia with a poorly enhancing loop.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Painful lump in the right groin and vomiting
inputs.hpi: 2 days of vomiting and colicky abdominal pain with distension; no flatus since yesterday. For the last 24 hours a painful lump in the right groin that she cannot push back. No previous abdominal surgery.

exam.abdomen: Distended, mildly tender centrally. Right groin: 3 cm tense, tender, irreducible lump below and lateral to the pubic tubercle with overlying erythema; no cough impulse.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Small bowel obstruction caused by an incarcerated right femoral hernia; the herniated loop is thick-walled with reduced enhancement. No free gas.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Strangulated right femoral hernia with small bowel obstruction
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Strangulated right femoral hernia causing small bowel obstruction — emergency repair with assessment of bowel viability.

socratesAnswers.site: Right groin lump and central abdomen
socratesAnswers.character: Colicky, now sharp over the lump

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: Web: PANE top 3: bowel obstruction, adhesive SBO, post-operative ileus. The SOCRATES site text 'Right groin lump' maps to groin_swelling but the obstruction features dominate; hernia appears only in the triage surgical match list. The 'hernia' symptom-branch details are not read by PANE.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: Let PANE read the hernia symptom branch ('Irreducible', 'Femoral') and exam chip 'Hernia present' as hernia_irreducible/groin_swelling evidence.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Painful lump in the right groin and vomiting' gives 'routine'.

mustExclude.note: WSES 2017: do not attempt reduction when strangulation is suspected (tender, erythematous, systemic signs, raised lactate) — non-viable bowel can be reduced into the abdomen.

guideline.name: WSES Bologna guidelines — adhesive small bowel obstruction (2017 update)
guideline.section: CT with IV contrast for strangulation signs; non-operative management (NGT, fluids) up to 72 h without strangulation; water-soluble contrast challenge (colon within 24 h predicts success); surgery for strangulation, peritonitis or failed NOM; virgin abdomen and hernia causes
guideline.citation: ten Broek RPG, Krielen P, Di Saverio S, et al. Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO): 2017 update of the evidence-based guidelines from the WSES ASBO working group. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:24.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias (2017 update)
guideline.section: Strangulation signs; emergency repair; manual reduction not attempted when strangulation is suspected
guideline.citation: Birindelli A, Sartelli M, Di Saverio S, et al. 2017 update of the WSES guidelines for emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias. World J Emerg Surg. 2017;12:37.

rationale: Permutation: hernia as the cause. Strangulated femoral hernia needs emergency repair; attempting manual reduction of a strangulated hernia is contraindicated.
